name: Peak-time scheduler to posted proof
looks: A schedule card shows a horizontal time-of-day track with a highlighted 'Peak' zone; a dot sits on the track and the time readout above updates as it is set, then a cursor presses 'Schedule'. The card blurs and resolves into a posted confirmation card with a checkmark, the original reply text, and live upvote and reply counts.
build: The track is an SVG/DOM line with tick labels; the peak zone is a soft highlighted band behind the dot's resting position, and the time readout is a live text set from the dot's x position. The transition between cards is a blur dissolve (gaussian filter radius tweened to 0) rather than a cut.
sound: A soft tick as the dot settles on peak, a click on Schedule, and a confirm chime as the posted card resolves.
prompt: Close the loop from decision to proof: a simple time-of-day picker highlights the best window to act and a single button commits to it, then the view resolves through a soft blur into a confirmation card showing the result already live, with real counts ticking on it.
